advances: A free-mass balanced linear source objective with a fixed prescribed slope, including arbitrary finite source families.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Let $F$ be the smallest face of $\operatorname{conv}P$ containing $j$ and put $V=\operatorname{span}(F-j)$. A functional exposing $F$ has maximum on $F$ and a strict gap at every $z\in P\setminus F$. Every balanced density, meaning $\int(z-j)f\,d\mu=0$, is therefore supported on $F$, since any positive mass on the other sites would contribute strictly negatively to the integral of the exposing functional centered at $j$.

Write $w_z=|K_z|$ and choose strictly positive numbers $\rho_z$ on $P\cap F$ summing to one with $\sum_z\rho_z z=j$. To see existence, let $\bar z$ be the average of all these bases; for small $\theta>0$ the point $(j-\theta\bar z)/(1-\theta)$ remains in $F$ because $j$ is in its relative interior. Express that point as a convex combination and mix in the uniform combination for $\bar z$ with weight $\theta$. Take $\eta_z=c\rho_z/w_z$ for a sufficiently small $c>0$. Then $\eta_z\in[\delta,1-\delta]$ for a common $\delta>0$, and $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}w_z\eta_z(z-j)=0$.

For the fixed prescribed $b$ minimize over $a\in V$ the function
$$
G(a)=\sum_{z\in P\cap F}\int_{K_z}[u\cdot x-b+a\cdot(z-j)]_+\,dx.
$$
The hinge is 1-Lipschitz. Thus $G(a)$ differs by at most the constant $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}\int_{K_z}|u\cdot x-b|\,dx$ from $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}w_z[a\cdot(z-j)]_+$. Subtract the identically zero sum $\sum_{z\in P\cap F}w_z\eta_z a\cdot(z-j)$ from the latter. Each remaining summand is at least $\delta w_z|a\cdot(z-j)|$. Their sum grows at least linearly with $\|a\|$ on $V$, since the vectors $z-j$ span $V$. Continuity gives a finite minimizer (if $V=\{0\}$ take $a=0$). The threshold levels are volume null on all positive fibers since $u\ne0$. Dominated differentiation gives that $\nabla G$ is the sum of the centered base moments of the cap over $F$ and belongs to $V$. At a minimizer it vanishes, so the cap indicator on $F$ is balanced.

This indicator uniquely maximizes $\int(u\cdot x-b)f\,d\mu$ over balanced $0\le f\le1$, of arbitrary mass. Indeed one can insert $a\cdot(z-j)$ in the integrand by balance and maximize pointwise, with strict identification off the null level. The supporting-plane inequality says that a feasible density at $(t_0,q_0)$ maximizes the same objective. Thus that density is the cap indicator and has the stated moments. If $F\ne\operatorname{conv}P$, add to $a$ a sufficiently large positive multiple of the exposing functional, centered through $a\cdot(z-j)$. It vanishes on $F$ and makes the margin negative on every off-face fiber by boundedness and finiteness. This leaves $b$ unchanged.
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

Fix $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ and $0<t_0<T_j$. If
$$
u\cdot q\le u\cdot q_0+b(t-t_0),\qquad u\ne0,
$$
is a supporting plane at $(t_0,q_0)$ of $\{(t,q):0\le t\le T_j,\ q\in Q_t(j)\}$, there is a finite $a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that $H=\{u\cdot x+a\cdot(z-j)-b\ge0\}$ satisfies
$$
\mu(H)=t_0,\qquad \int_H(z-j)\,d\mu=0,\qquad \int_H x\,d\mu=q_0.
$$
The scalar $b$ is the prescribed slope of the supporting plane.
title: Actual cap realization with prescribed raw-moment support slope
